flagged.evidence: Step 1.3 permits any field K, but step 2.3 asserts that 'rQ(t) has degree r with leading coefficient r'. Take K=F_2, r=2, z_1=0 and z_2=1. These points are distinct and Q(t)=t(t-1) is monic of degree 2, but rQ(t)=0. The opened dependency items/def-polynomial-degree-leading-coefficient-and-monic.md explicitly states: 'The zero polynomial has no degree and no leading coefficient.' Thus the asserted degree and leading coefficient do not exist. Coefficient cancellation still proves the needed support bound, and the later application over Q remains valid.

The carrier cites Chan, printed p. 29, as containing 'the bijection Theorem 8.6'. In the cited primary PDF, Theorem 8.6 instead concludes 'Then T− is again standard' after deletion. The correspondence bijection is Theorem 8.9 on printed p. 30. The named theorem therefore does not give the attributed result. Checked in [Chan's notes](https://web.math.princeton.edu/~charchan/RepresentationTheorySymmetricGroupsNotes.pdf), Theorems 8.6–8.9.

The carrier cites Martin, 'printed p. 205: the RSK subsequence theorem (Theorem 9.10.12)'. The cited PDF's Theorem 9.10.12, on printed p. 199, states: 'The Schur functions form an orthonormal Z-basis for Λ under the Hall inner product.' Printed p. 205 belongs to the alternant proof in Section 9.13. Neither the named theorem nor the named page supplies the attributed subsequence result. Checked in [Martin's notes](https://jeremymartinmath.github.io/CombinatoricsNotes.pdf).

The carrier attributes 'the recovery of the inserted element from a P-symbol' to Schensted, pp. 179–180. Those complete pages contain tableau and shape definitions, the hook formula and example, and the forward row/column insertion rules. The recovery argument appears in the proof of Lemma 3 on printed p. 182, using the recording tableau to identify the deletion corner. The cited pages do not contain the attributed recovery argument. Checked in [Schensted's article](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~billey/classes/561.fall.2019/articles/schensted.1961.pdf).

The carrier cites Schensted, 'p. 180: the recovery argument for the inserted element'. Printed p. 180 gives the hook computation and forward insertion definition; the upward recovery procedure occurs in Lemma 3's proof on printed p. 182. The stated locator does not supply the attributed argument. Checked in [Schensted's article](https://sites.math.washington.edu/~billey/classes/561.fall.2019/articles/schensted.1961.pdf), complete printed pp. 179–182.

The carrier attributes 'Corollary 1.15 at n=0,1' to Craven. The cited corollary on printed p. 13 expressly begins 'If n is a positive integer', so it excludes n=0. The example's direct empty-case verification is correct, but the source attribution extends the corollary beyond its stated domain. Checked in [Craven's notes](https://web.mat.bham.ac.uk/D.A.Craven/docs/lectures/groupsgeomreptheory2013.pdf), Corollary 1.15.
